subject: On-prem service naming, mutual TLS profile, and split-horizon DNS verification
messages:
From: Mary Jenkins <mary.jenkins@acme-cloud.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: netops@acme-cloud.com
Date: 2027-05-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: On-prem TLS & DNS for private endpoints — clarifying requirements

Connor / Marissa,

Thanks for the call this morning. Attached is our simplified network diagram (acme-network-diagram.pdf). A couple of things we need to lock down for our on-prem deployment of Redwood Private:

- Naming: we plan to expose application endpoints as app-<env>.acme.internal (split-horizon). We want to confirm best practice for service names versus tenant-specific aliases.
- TLS termination: Acme security prefers mutual TLS for control-plane RPCs and server-only TLS for user-facing endpoints. We need guidance on certificate provisioning and trust anchors.
- Verification: we must provide a reproducible verification checklist for our auditors (DNS assertions + cert chain proofs).

Can you outline the recommended mTLS profile, certificate pinning options, and verification steps? Also share any scripts or configs you use for the on-prem ACME sidecar pattern.

Thanks,
Mary
Mary Jenkins
Director, Cloud Platform — Acme Cloud

From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Mary Jenkins <mary.jenkins@acme-cloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-19T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem TLS & DNS for private endpoints — clarifying requirements

Hi Mary — thanks for the diagram, that's helpful. High-level answers below and attached a short machine-readable profile (redwood-mtls-profile.yaml) plus a verification checklist draft (verification-checklist.md).

1) Service naming
- Recommendation: canonical service FQDNs should be service.<env>.svc.acme.internal. Tenant or app aliases (app-<tenant>.acme.internal) are fine as CNAMEs that resolve to the canonical name in the split-horizon zone. This keeps routing consistent and lets us pin cert SANs to the canonical hostnames.

2) mTLS profile and trust model
- Control plane (internal RPCs): require mutual TLS. Use a short-lived client certificate profile (7-14 day TTL) rotated via the ACME sidecar or internal CA. Redwoods's runtime accepts client leaf certs signed by the customer root or an agreed intermediary.
- Data-plane (user endpoints): server-only TLS validated by customer clients. We support SAN-based certs (wildcard or multi-SAN) depending on scale.
- Pinning: for the strictest posture, we recommend pinning to the intermediate CA that signs the runtime leaf certs rather than leaf fingerprints. That avoids frequent re-pinning when we rotate leaf certs.

3) Certificate provisioning pattern
- Two supported flows: customer-managed internal CA (preferred for air-gapped/on-prem) or ACME sidecar that performs CSR + CA callout to your internal PKI. The sidecar stores the certs in a mounted volume and signals the runtime via a file-watch.

4) Verification checklist (attached)
- DNS: show split-horizon resolution from a client inside your VPC + from your auditor VM (steps included).
- TLS: validate full chain, OCSP/CRL where applicable, and confirm expected SANs.
- mTLS: run a test where a client without a valid cert is rejected; a valid cert succeeds.

Open questions for you:
- Do you require OCSP stapling for internal endpoints?
- Any constraints on TTLs for the split-horizon zone (we usually recommend >=30s for stability in our tests)?

I'll let Marissa and Karthik jump in with ops/runbook details.

—Connor
Connor O'Brien
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Mary Jenkins <mary.jenkins@acme-cloud.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-19T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem TLS & DNS for private endpoints — clarifying requirements

Adding a couple of operational notes from the on-prem side:

- ACME sidecar behavior: for on-prem customers we run the sidecar in 'pull' mode so your internal PKI mints certs and the sidecar polls/refreshes. That avoids outbound ACME calls from air-gapped clusters.
- File layout we expect (example): /var/run/redwood/certs/server.crt, server.key, chain.pem. If you use an HSM/KMS, we can integrate for key storage but the sidecar interface is the canonical signal to the runtime.
- Rotation window & blackout: schedule rotations in a 30‑minute maintenance window. Our runtime supports zero-downtime cert swaps when the chain is replaced atomically.

I'll attach a small TTL/test vector CSV (ttl-and-test-plan.csv) with recommended values and a simple curl/mTLS command that the NetOps team can run.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Product — Private Deploys, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Mary Jenkins <mary.jenkins@acme-cloud.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-19T16:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem TLS & DNS for private endpoints — clarifying requirements

Mary — quick technical steps and a short test plan (copying the checklist into email for visibility):

> 1) DNS: create split-horizon zone acme.internal. Internal view: create A records for service.<env>.svc.acme.internal -> private IPs. External view: no public records.
> 2) Certs: issue intermediate CA that signs runtime leaf certs. Upload intermediate CA to Redwood trust store (we'll provide an upload link or API).
> 3) mTLS handshake testing:
>    - Negative test: run openssl s_client -connect service.prod.svc.acme.internal:443 (no client cert) and confirm handshake fails with "handshake failure".
>    - Positive test: openssl s_client -connect service.prod.svc.acme.internal:443 -cert client.pem -key client.key -CAfile chain.pem -> check "Verify return code: 0 (ok)".
> 4) Chain pin validation: grab the DER of the intermediate and compute sha256 hash; compare against the expected pinned value in our runtime config.

Notes: For TTLs we suggest 30s for development, 300s for staging, 3600s for prod; lower TTLs increase DNS query volume during failover. I'll link the runtime config keys in the runbook: https://redwood.company/docs/runbooks/private-deploy-mtls

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: Mary Jenkins <mary.jenkins@acme-cloud.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-20T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem TLS & DNS for private endpoints — clarifying requirements

Thanks — this is exactly what our auditors needed. Couple of small follow-ups:

- We do want OCSP stapling for the user-facing endpoints; control plane can be without stapling if OCSP is impractical inside the air-gapped segments.
- Can you produce the intermediate fingerprint we should pin to? If you can add that to the verification-checklist.md we'll be able to sign off and route the change through our compliance tracker.

Also please send a DocuSign flow for the ops access agreement so our security team can grant Redwood the permission to pull certs via the sidecar in pull mode.

I'll review the TTLs with NetOps tomorrow.

Best,
Mary
